lastText: File ClosedA Republic Remembered by MarzabottoMajor DefeatItalian High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: APRIL 28, 1945 · filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathThe Italian Social Republic ends on April 28, 1945, twenty months after Mussolini's rescue from Gran Sasso installed it as a German client state in the occupied north. The human cost of this path runs higher than the historical one at nearly every hinge point: Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the higher tolls of any Axis power relative to population. War was declared on Britain alone, months after France had already settled its own armistice without Italian participation: a different opening than the historical one, fought for the Mediterranean prize directly rather than for a seat at a peace table that no longer existed to claim. Graziani ordered the withdrawal from the fortified camps before Compass's flanking attack landed, rather than holding as the historical delay did: sparing the Tenth Army the worst of a rout that historically cost some 130,000 men taken prisoner. Malta was taken in an actual 1940 invasion, while the garrison was still weak, then lost back to a determined British counter-effort over the following winter, the documented British commitment to the island reasserting itself even against an early and successful Italian gamble.
